notes: Iteration 3 baseline is no-skill (same as prior iterations).
Three discriminating assertions were added this iteration: EARS phrasing, Given/When/Then + REQ traceability, and a 'For Implementing Agents' handoff block.
Timing/token metrics were not present in subagent completion notifications, so this benchmark compares output quality only.
Baseline avoided skill files and invented a ticket schema that contradicts the real lifecycle; no EARS, no GWT traceability, no handoff block.
Non-discriminating: the baseline reads SKILL.md v1.2 as its subject and mirrors EARS/GWT/handoff conventions even without loading the skill as operating instructions.
Strong grounding and scoping, but no EARS, no GWT traceability, no handoff block; set status 'Ready for Review' despite open questions.
with_skill: 30/30 assertions passed (100%) across the three test cases.

without_skill: 23/30 assertions passed (76.7%). The 7 misses are concentrated in the three new discriminating assertions (EARS, GWT traceability, handoff block) plus one grounding miss on the ticket-validation baseline.

Delta +23pt overall, but this understates the effect: eval-1 is confounded (baseline reads the skill as subject material), so on the two clean evals (0 and 2) the skill delta is +0.6 and +0.3 respectively.
The three new assertions are strongly discriminating on evals 0 and 2 (skill passes all three; both baselines fail all three) and non-discriminating on eval 1.
Recommendation: replace or drop eval-1 as a value discriminator, or swap its subject for an artifact that does not already embody EARS/GWT/handoff conventions.
